question.text: Aditya is a 24-year-old single BPO employee with a high-risk profile. He has Rs. 10,00,000 to invest. Based on the model portfolio for his profile, how much should he allocate to sector funds?

explanation.text: The Logic: The model portfolio for the young BPO / high-risk profile allocates 20% to sector funds. 20% of Rs. 10,00,000 = Rs. 2,00,000. The full source allocation is 50% diversified equity (Rs. 5,00,000), 20% sector funds (Rs. 2,00,000), 10% gold ETF (Rs. 1,00,000), 10% debt / fixed deposits (Rs. 1,00,000) and 10% short-term debt / liquid / bank (Rs. 1,00,000). The Trap: Rs. 5,00,000 (Option A) is the diversified-equity line (50%), not sector funds. Rs. 3,50,000 (Option D) is the equity allocation for the moderate-risk young married family model (35%). The arithmetic is straightforward once the correct line of the correct model portfolio is identified. Note: The 20% sector allocation is taken directly from the source model portfolio for this profile; it is not characterised by the workbook as either a cap or as aggressive on its own.
